column22: Preprint representation of the Oenothera harringtonii RNA-seq study retained as published SCHPRISMA-000205 for report-level provenance only.

decision_note: Ecology source records pollinator visits pollen transfer fruit set and nectar piercing across 14 plots and three disturbance patch types.

Petunia study resolves pollination-syndrome traits and pollen scent but does not measure a focal plant-antagonist response to the same floral coordinate in the current experiment.
Phylogeographic floral-scent variation is informative for trait history but the frozen report does not supply a focal antagonist receiver response or conflict attribution.

A_trait: floral fragrance flower size and display
claim_ceiling: Outcrossing-to-selfing transition is associated with about 99 percent fragrance reduction but is not shared-cue to private-cue evolution
decision_note: Abronia field/common-garden study shows genetic differentiation and dramatic fragrance vestigialization after the mating-system transition.

column22: Drought manipulation measures floral-trait plasticity in an animal-pollinated plant but no focal herbivore/antagonist response is measured.

claim_ceiling: Floral odors and pollination-seed-predation outcomes converge by elevation but A is not randomized
decision_note: Haplopappus source combines floral VOCs insect olfactory bioassay fertilized seeds and predated seeds along an Andean elevation gradient.

column22: Multi-state palm-squirrel natural-history synthesis classifies nectar robbing/flower predation/visitation but does not test a declared floral trait coordinate.
New Phytologist article is a review/synthesis of floral volatile information transfer and is retained only for source chasing.
Agricultural-landscape dissertation integrates pollinators pests and natural enemies but the focal drivers are landscape/community processes rather than one floral attraction coordinate.

decision_note: Open thesis tests floral asymmetry and ant-plant effects on floral visitors and reports ant-density-dependent reproductive fitness.

claim_ceiling: Fragrance-associated ant attraction predicts pollinator disruption and reduced fruit set but fragrance itself is not randomized
decision_note: Artabotrys source links floral volatiles to weaver-ant attraction and reports ant interference with pollinator visits and lower fruit set.

column22: Protea neighbourhood study integrates pollinator- and seed-predator-mediated fecundity but the focal coordinate is neighbourhood/community structure rather than a floral A.

decision_note: Ipomopsis warming experiment measures floral VOCs display rewards and fly seed-predator oviposition across sites and years.

column22: Chilopsis study uses nectar robbing itself as the exposure and does not identify an independent floral attraction/display coordinate A.

A_trait: virus-induced floral VOC colour and reward state
claim_ceiling: Virus-induced floral changes improve pollinator attraction and seed recovery but do not show an antagonist receiver reading the same A
decision_note: Cambridge thesis manipulates virus infection and measures VOC/color/reward changes bee behavior pollination and seed production.

column22: Juniperus study combines wind-pollination efficiency and predispersal seed predators; it lacks an animal pollinator mutualist receiver for the SCH shared-audience question.
Oecologia Australis article is explicitly a review of floral VOC roles in plant-insect interactions rather than an independent primary study.
Plant Physiology piece is a feature/commentary on allelic variation in floral odor rather than the independent primary experiment.
Castilleja study documents floral-visitor networks after historical herbivore removal but does not measure a current plant-antagonist response to a floral A.

A_trait: floral attractiveness morphology and enemy-avoidance syndrome

decision_note: Datura common-garden experiment manipulates herbivory/water and measures floral phenotype and genetic outcrossing rate.

claim_ceiling: A novel scent pathway with opposite audience functions is recovered but not a reconstructed shared-cue to private-cue transition
decision_note: Molecular Biology and Evolution source identifies the biosynthetic origin of benzylacetone which attracts pollinators and deters florivores.

column22: bioRxiv representation of the published Nicotiana benzylacetone study retained as SCHPRISMA-000285.

column22: Annals of Botany article is a review/meta-analytic synthesis of nectar evolutionary ecology rather than an independent primary study.
